To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The thermal performance of housing specifically designed for older citizens is not consistent across the dwellings.

the energy efficiency of buildings specifically designed to house older people is not the same as the energy efficiency of other buildings, that the energy efficiency varies between dwellings within these building, and that the energy performance of these buildings impacts the internal temperatures and energy bills of the occupants.
The thermal performance of the dwellings in the sample was not uniform, with some being very well performing, others performing poorly and the remainder performing somewhere in the middle.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the energy efficiency of dwellings built specifically for the elderly and the implications of the findings for energy policy, the energy performance of dwellings and occupant health.
understanding how the energy efficiency of dwellings designed for older people can impact the health and economic security of the occupants.

understanding the interplay between housing specifically designed for the elderly and energy efficiency, and the impact this has on the internal temperatures of these dwellings and the economic security of the occupants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
energy efficiency of housing for the older people does not matter.
housing for the elderly should be built with the thermal efficiency of dwellings as a priority and that this will have a positive impact on their health and economic security.
the thermal efficiency and internal comfort of the dwellings are not the same across the sample of buildings.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the thermal efficiency requirements of buildings designed specifically for older people should not be the same as for other buildings.
there is a need to better understand the energy efficiency of dwellings specifically designed for older citizens, and how this can be improved.
the energy efficiency of the housing for older people is important and should be considered in the design and construction of these dwellings, as well as when considering energy efficiency policy.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the energy performance of a building, in terms of the thermal performance of the building envelope and the heating and cooling systems, is not the same in all buildings and this has an impact on the internal temperature of the building and the health and economic security of occupants, especially those with low incomes.
the energy performance of housing for older people is a critical issue that requires further investigation.

energy efficiency of housing for the elderly is not just a matter of energy performance of dwellings, but also a matter of the thermal performance of the dwellings and the impact this has on the health, economic security and wellbeing of older citizens.
